title: Mass automated login attempts hit Germany's BundID citizen accounts; accounts blocked as a precaution
date_note: Date of the reports; the attack started before this day.
summary: Unknown attackers ran an automated wave of login attempts against BundID, Germany's federal digital citizen account, trying to take over accounts in bulk. Per dpa and Handelsblatt, citing the BSI, protective measures triggered, affected accounts were blocked and holders were told to set a new password. Officials say they have no evidence data was taken or profiles entered; no numbers were given.
plain: Attackers tried to break into many German citizen accounts used for government services. Protections held and affected accounts were locked; officials see no sign of data theft.
exec: A national government login service was targeted at scale; account lockouts may disrupt public-service access.
action: BundID users: set a new, unique password if you receive a block notice, and enable stronger login methods where offered.

validation.note: Channelpartner and Volksstimme (dpa) read; both cite the BSI via Handelsblatt, so they are close to one report, and a Digital Ministry spokesperson confirmed details. Golem page text did not load.
